verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time... Floating in the Pacific Ocean on Friday'; R3: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) off the coast of San Diego'; R4: 'Splashdown confirmed at 7:07 p.m. Central time, 5:07 p.m. Pacific time' (equivalent to 8:07 EDT); URLs dated 2026/04/10.
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm date, time in EDT equivalent, location in Pacific Ocean off San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concluded a 10-day trip around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'nearly 10-day flight'; R3: launch 'April 1' to splashdown 'April 10'; R4: 'nearly 10-day journey'; R5: 'after 10-day mission'; R6: '10-day mission'.
verifications.reasoning: Launch April 1 to splashdown April 10 spans 10 days; consistently described as 10-day or nearly 10-day mission around the moon.

verifications.claim: Full video coverage of the Artemis II reentry and splashdown, including the Orion capsule's parachute deployment, is available on PBS, WBAL-TV, and the NASA YouTube channel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (PBS): 'Watch in our video player above' for splashdown after re-entry; R3 (NASA): 'Watch live return coverage... on NASA’s YouTube channel'; R4 (WBAL-TV): 'FULL VIDEO: Watch Artemis II crew splashdown... From parachute deployment to splashdown'.
verifications.reasoning: Each specified source provides video coverage explicitly including reentry/splashdown and parachute deployment as described.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed west of San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'waters off San Diego'; R2: 'off the San Diego coast'; R3: 'off the coast of San Diego' in Pacific Ocean.
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm splashdown off San Diego coast in Pacific, which is west of San Diego.

verifications.claim: Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen returned safely.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen... All four astronauts were able to walk'; R2: 'Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Canada's Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; all note safe return.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew names listed across sources; explicitly stated as safe, healthy, walking post-recovery.

verifications.claim: Videos of the Artemis II reentry and splashdown show the fiery reentry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6 (video): 'Watch the Artemis II re-entry: Separation, blackout, then splashdown'; R2: 'engulfed in red-hot plasma during peak heating'; R1: 'heat enveloping the spacecraft created a blackout... plasma'.
verifications.reasoning: Video sources cover re-entry including blackout (fiery plasma phase); descriptions confirm fiery reentry visuals.

verifications.claim: Videos of the Artemis II reentry and splashdown show the deployment of parachutes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'From parachute deployment to splashdown, watch the full historic moment'; R3: timeline 'drogue parachutes will deploy... three main parachutes will deploy'; R1: 'small parachutes known as drogues deployed. The main parachutes were released'.
verifications.reasoning: Video pages explicitly include parachute deployment footage; timelines confirm.

verifications.claim: Videos of the Artemis II reentry and splashdown show the final splashdown into the Pacific.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (PBS): 'Watch... crew splashes down'; R4 (WBAL-TV): 'FULL VIDEO: Watch Artemis II crew splashdown in Pacific Ocean'; R5 (NBC): 'Artemis II splashes down in Pacific Ocean'; R6 (BBC): 'splashdown'.
verifications.reasoning: All listed video sources are titled and describe showing the splashdown in Pacific.

verifications.claim: A joint NASA and U.S. military team was on-site to retrieve the Orion capsule and crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'combined NASA and U.S. military recovery team... extract the crew from Orion'; R2: 'NASA and the Defense Department teamed up... recovery ship USS John P. Murtha'; R1: 'recovery team... U.S.S. John P. Murtha'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state joint NASA/U.S. military recovery teams retrieved capsule and crew on-site off San Diego.
